key_points: Problem (PD-1): dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1,220/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-05). Investigation shifted the framing away from the requester's response-handling-gap claim (CL-01, hypothesis H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING rejected by E-06) toward a billing-import/calculation defect on ACTUAL-read bills, since 59% of disputed bills (1,785/3,025) involve ACTUAL, non-estimated reads (E-02, H-ACTUAL-READ-BILL-ERROR SUPPORTED).
The problem-definition gate for PD-1 returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring unresolved questions as verification obligations (VOBs) rather than fully resolving them before proceeding.
Release decision is HOLD. Reason: critical VOB-R-3 is OPEN, required BEFORE_RELEASE, and blocks the ENTIRE_SOLUTION, intersecting the release scope at review_field_route_completion:DA-ROUTE.
The only work actually executed/packaged was review_field_route_completion:DA-ROUTE (route-log lagging_routes, 14 routes, E-09), matching the solution design's minimum_useful_scope and release_scope.

A verification run (seq 200) flagged a semantic contradiction: the proposed SR-R4 remedy (field-dispatch route-priority change) still targets ESTIMATED-read accounts under a field-incompleteness premise, but E-11 shows 1,184 of 1,240 of those disputes are AMI-channel reads rejected by billing import for high consumption, not missing field reads; the system's own REPLAN (seq 189) called this a 'solution-path contradiction'.

No automated bill adjustments or route-dispatch pushes were made in this release; K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH human-approval constraints remain intact, and the true root-cause fix (SR-R2) has no domain_authorization for billing-config writes and is infeasible in contest time.

Two high-impact unknowns, VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-TIMING and VOB-U-SURGE-PERIOD-ALIGNMENT, remain OPEN and continue to block the billing-rules, billing-defect, and ticket-analysis portions of the original scope from release.

limitations_explained: The problem definition only reached a conditional pass; some open questions were deferred as tracked verification obligations instead of being settled before work proceeded.

The field-dispatch route-priority remedy (SR-R4) is contradicted by evidence: it assumes estimated-read disputes come from incomplete field routes, but E-11 shows they are mostly caused by billing-import rejecting high-consumption AMI reads, so this remedy has not been revised to match the evidence.

Whether a billing rule actually changed around August (VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-TIMING) and whether the disputed-bills breakdown truly aligns with the Aug-Sep surge window (VOB-U-SURGE-PERIOD-ALIGNMENT) are both still open, high-impact questions blocking the rules/defect/ticket-analysis portions of the investigation.

Even if the exact faulty billing rule were found, fixing it (SR-R2) is not something this release can do: it is infeasible within the available time and no one has authorization to write to the billing-config system; any correction must go through Billing Operations change control (SH-BILL), never an automated agent.
Dispute response-time performance is already inside its 3.0-day SLA target (E-06), so an auto-answer agent cannot meaningfully improve that aspect of the problem.
The health of the billing-config tool is unknown, so any attempt to pin down the exact defective rule (SR-R1) may fail or return incomplete results.

The AMI/MDMS export system was degraded and already placed on hold pending vendor-provisioned access, with no fallback, so AMI-read verification against the route-completion data (DA-MDMS) could not be included in this release.

The staffing-shortage explanation behind the route-priority remedy comes from a single stakeholder (SH-FIELD) with a disclosed incentive bias, and it remains unverified whether field route incompleteness meaningfully contributes to the estimated-read disputes at all.
proposal.summary: The problem was defined as a doubling of billing dispute tickets (from ~600/month to ~1,220/month, E-05) that the requester (SH-CS, CL-01) framed as a response-handling gap needing an auto-answer AI agent. Evidence instead showed response times are within SLA (E-06), no tariff change occurred (E-03/E-04), and 59% of disputed bills are tied to ACTUAL, not estimated, meter reads (E-02), pointing to a billing-import/calculation defect rather than a read-collection or response-speed problem. This reframed root problem (PD-1) passed its definition gate only CONDITIONALLY, with several questions deferred as verification obligations (VOBs). The release itself is a HOLD: a critical, OPEN verification obligation (VOB-R-3) is required to be resolved BEFORE_RELEASE and directly intersects the one piece of work that was actually completed and packaged — the field route completion review (review_field_route_completion:DA-ROUTE, based on route-log's 14 lagging routes, E-09). That obligation exists because a later analysis (E-11) found that most ESTIMATED-read disputes are caused by billing-import rejecting high-consumption AMI reads, not by incomplete field routes — directly undercutting the field-dispatch route-priority remedy (SR-R4) that this work item was meant to support, a contradiction the system's own replan (seq 189) and verification step (seq 200) both flagged. No bill adjustments or dispatch changes were executed; those remain gated by human-approval constraints (K-BILLWRITE, K-DISPATCH). Several other parts of the original investigation scope (billing-rules, billing-defect, ticket-type analysis, AMI read delivery) remain excluded or blocked by other open unknowns and a degraded AMI export tool, and the real root-cause fix (correcting the billing-config rule) is explicitly left for Billing Operations to do manually, not for any automated agent.
